first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6%. Memory 86 showed that shortening onboarding improved completion rates and adoption across self-serve. Memory 31 demonstrated that signup simplification lifted first-week activation in SMB. These form a coherent case for testing simplified onboarding as the immediate lever. I'm verifying memory 86 to confirm the causal strength and any segment conditions, and memory 73 to calibrate why promotional pricing (though effective for acquisition) carries retention risk and should be the fallback, not the lead. A small guarded test on onboarding simplification is lower-risk than broad promotional pricing, aligns with the observed metric decline, and can generate sustainable engagement lift without the 30-day retention penalty seen in pricing work. This preserves the option to escalate to pricing or sales-assist if simplification underperforms.
